shouldFix.title: Gate the leftover execution property, not ownership of the originating DR-133 law
shouldFix.finding: V4 quotes the full G20/G21 cells and acknowledges the relevant harness/evidence overlap, but every class then asks whether an existing gate 'ownsTheDR133Law'. That is not D-056's gate-3 test. Once an accepted architecture contract leaves only test execution, D-056 asks whether each execution remainder is already named as a condition-4 / DR-G* obligation with an owner. Its canonical DR-102 example routes CC-1..CC-11 execution to G21 while the non-translation/control-protocol law remains DR-102-owned; file 08 repeats that the hostile-conformance execution, not the architecture law, rides G21. V4's reasons therefore do not defeat a gate join: saying that unknown-Finding refusal is a DR-133 product law, relation-registry admission is DR-133, or Coverage-domain admission is DR-133 does not show that G21 cannot execute the malformed/candidate-discard/Coverage/D9 pass properties as condition-4 evidence. The same category error affects G20: its live retained evidence says 'no ... final authority' and its adopted D-086 execution text says the first-party TypeScript provider has no authority escape, yet V4 treats those as merely adjacent to NT-4/NT-7; NT-6 is not even checked against G20 despite G20's execution text expressly naming exit plus no authority escape. The class-by-class join records overlap but never tests whether the complete NT execution pass can be hosted by G20, G21, or their combined evidence surfaces.
shouldFix.impact: The subject's sole positive act is a measured conclusion that all seven NT executions need a new DR-G* obligation. Because it applies a stricter and irrelevant whole-law-ownership criterion, that conclusion is not established and CODEX-PONGJ-V3-SF1 is not substantively landed. The under-assignment is conservative and the candidate claims no closure, eligibility, or SATISFIED state, so this remains SHOULD-FIX rather than a blocker.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: For each NT, compare its executable input and complete pass property—not ownership of the DR-133 architecture law—to the full G20/G21 Claim, Harness, Required retained evidence, and Owner cells. Route the execution to an existing gate wherever that condition-4 obligation can carry the pass property, use a combined/split route where different conjuncts ride different gates, and identify a new DR-G* obligation only for a precisely stated residual. If rejecting G20/G21 for a class, name the exact pass conjunct their full cells cannot execute; source-law ownership alone is not a valid rejection.

summary: REJECT at 0 blockers and 1 SHOULD-FIX. V4 accurately quotes the complete live G20 and G21 cells, records their D-086 execution text, preserves all non-binding and no-SAT boundaries, and assigns no property to a gate whose claim cannot support it. But it does not land the prior join defect: it asks whether G20/G21 own the DR-133 product law, whereas D-056 gate 3 asks whether the leftover test execution rides a named condition-4 obligation with an owner. The adopted DR-102-to-G21 route demonstrates that these are different questions. V4 acknowledges exact malformed, candidate-discard, Coverage, D9/exit, final-authority, and authority-escape overlap but dismisses it on source-law ownership rather than testing the NT execution passes. A corrected execution-remainder join is required before ACCEPT.
